questions.prompt: Which is an example of civic participation outside elections?
choices: Public testimony, litigation, journalism, organizing, service, petition, or administrative comment
Assuming every institution has the same authority
questions.explanation: Civic participation includes many channels beyond voting and campaigns.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 35

questions.prompt: Why should jurisdiction be identified before advocacy?
choices: Because a persuasive request can fail if directed to an institution that lacks legal authority to act
Because local government cannot make policy
questions.explanation: Effective civic action requires directing requests to institutions with the relevant legal or administrative authority.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 35

questions.prompt: Which evaluation of a public-opinion poll is strongest?
choices: Check sample design, question wording, denominator, timing, and uncertainty before generalizing.
Assume a large percentage proves the policy is constitutional.
Reject every poll that has sampling error.
questions.explanation: Polling evidence requires methodological evaluation and cannot alone settle constitutional or normative questions.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 35

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a policy proposal from a slogan?
choices: A policy proposal identifies authority, mechanism, stakeholders, costs, rights, implementation, and measurable outcomes.
questions.explanation: Operational policy design specifies how action would occur, who is affected, and how results will be evaluated.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 35

Using consistent evidentiary and procedural standards across competing viewpoints
Treating every claim as equally supported
questions.explanation: Nonpartisan inquiry applies the same standards regardless of viewpoint while allowing explicit discussion of values and tradeoffs.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 35

shortResponse.prompt: Using at least two specific pieces of evidence, answer: How can citizens influence public policy without sacrificing accuracy, pluralism, or constitutional rights?
shortResponse.exemplar: A full-credit response states a defensible claim, uses two accurate details, explains how each supports the claim, and acknowledges one complexity or limitation.
